s1.p1: 1.1. The platform connects service providers and customers in order to streamline day-to-day operations and improve digital business efficiency.
s1.p2: 1.2. Use of the Site, the App, and the System is subject to these Terms of Use, as well as any applicable law and regulation in the United States. Accessing or using BizUply's services constitutes your full and binding consent to comply with all provisions of this Agreement. If you do not agree to these terms, you must not use the Site, the App, or any of the Company's services.
s1.p3: 1.3. The Company reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to change, amend, update, or remove parts of these terms at any time, with or without prior notice. Any update takes effect immediately upon posting on the Site. Continued use of the platform after such a change constitutes full acceptance of the updated terms.
s1.p4: 1.4. These terms are written in English and may from time to time be translated for convenience into other languages. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between translations, the English version shall prevail.
s1.p5: 1.5. These terms are drafted in the masculine form for grammatical convenience only and apply equally to all genders, individuals, and entities.
s1.p6: 1.6. BizUply operates under the laws of the United States. Unless otherwise stated, the law governing all matters relating to the platform, its use, and any dispute arising therefrom shall be the laws of the State of Delaware, United States, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles.
s1.p7: 1.7. This acknowledgment does not waive a privacy or consumer right that the mandatory law of the user's country does not allow a contract to waive.

s2.intro: For the purposes of this Agreement, the following definitions shall apply:

“The Company” – BizUply LLC, the operator and owner of the platform, including its affiliates, employees, partners, and contractors.
“The Site” / “The App” – BizUply's digital system, including all websites, domains, databases, APIs, code, infrastructure, interfaces, and related digital assets owned or managed by BizUply.
“The User” – any person, professional, business, organization, or other legal entity that accesses or uses the services for business management, communication, or collaboration purposes.
“Service Provider” / “Business” – any registered business or independent professional using the platform to create a business profile, manage appointments, customers, tasks, or communication through BizUply.
“Customer” – any person or entity that interacts with a business or service provider through the BizUply platform.
“The Services” – all features and functions provided by BizUply, including but not limited to CRM tools, messaging, appointment scheduling, automation, AI-driven insights, analytics, reputation management, collaboration tools, reviews, ratings, and business-page creation.
“Content” – any data, media, or material submitted, uploaded, transmitted, or displayed on the platform, including text, images, videos, logos, reviews, reports, analytics, or other user-generated material.
“Agreement” – this Terms of Use document, which constitutes a legally binding agreement between the User and BizUply.

s3.p1: 3.1. BizUply provides an advanced Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platform for the comprehensive management of small and medium-sized businesses (“SMBs”). list: Customer relationship management (CRM) for customers and leads
Internal messaging and communication between businesses and customers
Calendar, booking, and appointment-scheduling tools
A verified reviews system and star ratings for customer feedback
Customizable business pages with descriptions, service lists, images, and FAQs
Features for task management, reminders, and follow-ups
Collaboration tools between businesses for shared growth opportunities
An AI-powered business advisor for recommendations and smart automation
Analytics dashboards and performance reports for optimization

s5.p7: 5.7. The Site and the App use cookies and similar technologies for basic functionality, security, and the measurement described in section 5.9. Section 5.9 states which measurement tool loads and on which page.
s5.p8: 5.8. Users may disable or restrict cookies through their browser settings; however, as a result, certain features of the platform may not function properly.
s5.p9: 5.9. This paragraph describes the client code proposed for deployment, not the public site before that deployment. That code does not load Google Analytics, Google Tag Manager, or reCAPTCHA. The Meta Pixel, identifier 1427327632368128, is not loaded on a published customer site. On platform pages served from index.html, the pixel is loaded only when the cookie bizuply_tracking equals all. If the cookie is missing or equals essential, that page does not load the pixel, and choosing essential after the pixel has loaded reloads the page and clears the measurement cookies. The marketing homepage is still served from marketing.html, and that file in the same client code loads the pixel after the browser is idle without reading the cookie. A checkout event is sent from registration only when the cookie equals all and the pixel function is already present. Cloudflare Turnstile is loaded only on a screen that has a site key configured. A third-party tool that does load may set its own cookies under its own policy.
s5.p10: For more information about how BizUply collects, uses, and protects data, please review our detailed Privacy Policy, which forms an integral part of these Terms of Use.

s7.mandatoryLaw: 7.12. Sections 7.2, 7.3, 7.4, and 13 do not waive a refund or cancellation right that a mandatory consumer law gives a particular customer. For a consumer in the United States, the Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act, 15 U.S.C. § 8403, makes it unlawful to charge for an internet negative-option feature unless the material terms are clearly disclosed before billing information is taken, the consumer gives express informed consent, and a simple mechanism is provided to stop recurring charges. The FTC's 2024 expanded Negative Option Rule, including click-to-cancel, was vacated by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit on 8 July 2025, and the FTC restored the pre-2024 rule effective 12 February 2026. That expanded rule is not stated here as a law in force. For a consumer in California, Business and Professions Code § 17602 requires automatic-renewal disclosures, affirmative consent, and cancellation information when that statute applies. For a consumer in the European Union, Directive 2011/83/EU provides a 14-day withdrawal right for a distance contract unless an Article 16 exception applies, including the digital-content exception only when its consent and acknowledgment conditions are met. These laws are not described as applying to every customer. Where one applies, it controls over a contrary no-refund sentence. The no-refund wording above is kept as the company's position for customers to whom no such mandatory right applies.

privacyPage.intro: This Privacy Policy explains how BizUply collects, stores, uses, and protects personal and business information across the platform.
privacyPage.overviewText: Quickly navigate between the sections on privacy, data, security, user rights, and legal terms.

s1.p1: This Privacy Policy explains how BizUply, privately owned and operated under the laws of the United States, collects, stores, uses, and protects the personal information of its users and business customers (“Users,” “Businesses,” or “you”). By using the BizUply platform, you agree to the terms described in this document.
s1.p2: Bizuply LLC is a limited liability company formed in Delaware, United States. It provides business-management software, customer communication, and AI features when those features are used. The prior public text said the platform is headquartered in New York. That headquarters was not verified, and no street address is stated.
s1.p3: This Privacy Policy applies to all of our products, services, websites, and applications (the “Platform”) and describes in detail how we process data, what information we collect, and what rights you have with respect to your information.
s1.p4: By accessing or using our Platform, you acknowledge that you have read and understood this Privacy Policy. If you do not agree, please do not use BizUply or any of its services.

It does not state that the company complies with United States federal privacy law, New York privacy law, the GDPR, or the CCPA. A named law applies only when its own conditions are met. No compliance audit was completed.
s2.p3: This policy does not apply to third-party services, links, or integrations that are not owned or operated by BizUply. We encourage you to review their privacy policies before engaging with them.

revisions.proposed: 7.12. Sections 7.2, 7.3, 7.4, and 13 do not waive a refund or cancellation right that a mandatory consumer law gives a particular customer. For a consumer in the United States, the Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act, 15 U.S.C. § 8403, makes it unlawful to charge for an internet negative-option feature unless the material terms are clearly disclosed before billing information is taken, the consumer gives express informed consent, and a simple mechanism is provided to stop recurring charges. The FTC's 2024 expanded Negative Option Rule, including click-to-cancel, was vacated by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit on 8 July 2025, and the FTC restored the pre-2024 rule effective 12 February 2026. That expanded rule is not stated here as a law in force. For a consumer in California, Business and Professions Code § 17602 requires automatic-renewal disclosures, affirmative consent, and cancellation information when that statute applies. For a consumer in the European Union, Directive 2011/83/EU provides a 14-day withdrawal right for a distance contract unless an Article 16 exception applies, including the digital-content exception only when its consent and acknowledgment conditions are met. These laws are not described as applying to every customer. Where one applies, it controls over a contrary no-refund sentence. The no-refund wording above is kept as the company's position for customers to whom no such mandatory right applies.
revisions.why: No-refund text is kept, and it yields where a mandatory consumer statute applies.
revisions.source: 15 U.S.C. § 8403; Eighth Circuit vacatur, 8 July 2025; FTC restoration effective 12 February 2026; Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 17602; Directive 2011/83/EU arts. 9 and 16. Checked 6 November 2026.
